Multi Agent 10. Commands 11. Anti Patterns 12. Community What Is Claude Code ? An agentic coding tool that reads your codebase, edits files, runs commands, and integrates with your development tools. Core Concept Not Autocomplete — An Agent Claude Code doesn't just suggest completions. It thinks through problems, explores codebases, plans changes, executes solutions, runs tests, and iterates — all autonomously within a single conversation. 🖥️ Terminal-Native Power Claude Code lives where developers live. It operates directly in your terminal with full access to your tools, filesystem, and shell — no context switching needed. It's built to be your pair programmer in the environment you already use. 🧠 Agentic Architecture Powered by an agentic loop: Claude reads context, decides which tool to use, executes it, observes results, and repeats until the task is done. It can chain dozens of actions — reading files, running commands, editing code — all without manual intervention. 🔌 Available Everywhere Use Claude Code in your Terminal, VS Code, Cursor, JetBrains IDEs, the Desktop App, on the Web (claude.ai/code), via iOS, through GitHub Actions, GitLab CI/CD, Slack, and even Chrome. Capabilities What You Can Do Build Features & Fix Bugs Describe what you want, and Claude explores the codebase, identifies the right files, implements changes, writes tests, and verifies everything works. Automate Git Workflow Create commits with descriptive messages, open pull requests, handle code reviews, and even respond to PR comments — all through natural language. claude "commit my changes with a descriptive message" Write & Run Tests Find untested code, generate test scaffolding, add edge cases, run the suite, and fix any failures — all in one prompt. claude "write tests for the auth module, run them, and fix any failures" Connect External Tools (MCP) Use the Model Context Protocol to connect Claude to databases, monitoring tools, issue trackers, documentation sites, and any API. Run Agent Teams Coordinate multiple Claude instances working in parallel — one writes code, another reviews, a third writes tests. Experimental agent teams with a lead coordinator. Pipe, Script & Automate Use Claude as a Unix utility: pipe in logs, diff outputs, or file lists. Process them headlessly and chain into your existing command-line workflows. git diff main --name-only | claude -p "review these changed files for security issues" Ecosystem Use Claude Code Everywhere Terminal VS Code JetBrains Desktop App Web (claude.ai/code) iOS App GitHub Actions GitLab CI/CD Slack Chrome Extension Agent SDK Claude Code Mastery Guide · Source: Anthropic Docs ← Learning OS Getting Started in 60 Seconds Install and start using Claude Code immediately on any platform. Installation Choose Your Platform 🍎 macOS / Linux curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash Or via Homebrew: brew install --cask claude-code # Upgrade later with: brew upgrade claude-code 🪟 Windows irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex Or via WinGet: winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode # Upgrade later with: winget upgrade Anthropic.ClaudeCode 💻 VS Code / Cursor Open Extensions ( Cmd+Shift+X / Ctrl+Shift+X ) Search for anthropic.claude-code Install and activate via Cmd+Shift+P / Ctrl+Shift+P 🖥️ Desktop App Download from macOS (Intel & Apple Silicon) or Windows (x64) . Requires a paid Claude subscription. 🌐 Web Go to claude.ai/code — run Claude Code on Anthropic's cloud infrastructure in isolated VMs. No local installation needed. 🔧 JetBrains Install the Claude Code plugin from the JetBrains Marketplace. Works with IntelliJ, PyCharm, WebStorm, and all JetBrains IDEs. First Session Your First 5 Minutes Navigate & Launch cd your-project claude Initialize Project Memory Create a CLAUDE.md that gives Claude persistent memory of your project: > /init Explore Your Codebase > give me an overview of this codebase > explain the main architecture patterns used here > how is authentication handled? Make Your First Change > add input validation to the user registration endpoint. write tests and run them to verify. 💡 Pro Tip Run /init in every new project. It's the single most impactful setup step. Claude will analyze your project structure and generate a tailored CLAUDE.md with conventions, commands, and patterns. 🔑 Authentication You'll need a Claude subscription (Pro, Team, or Enterprise) or an Anthropic Console API key. Third-party providers like AWS Bedrock and Google Vertex AI are also supported. Claude Code Mastery Guide · Source: Anthropic Docs The Golden Workflow Explore → Plan → Implement → Commit. The four-phase approach Anthropic engineers use internally for maximum effectiveness. The Framework Four Phases of Effective Development This is how Anthropic's own engineers work with Claude Code. Don't skip phases — each one builds on the previous. 1. Explore — Understand Before Changing Ask Claude to read and understand the existing code before making any changes. Let it map dependencies, trace execution flows, and identify relevant patterns. read /src/auth and understand how we handle sessions and login. also look at how we manage environment variables for secrets. Point Claude to specific directories. Be precise about what you want it to understand. Don't just say "look at the project." 2. Plan — Think Before Acting Use Plan Mode ( Shift+Tab twice or Ctrl+G ) to prevent Claude from writing code. Get a structured implementation plan and review it carefully. I want to add Google OAuth. What files need to change? What's the session flow? Create a plan. Why Plan Mode Matters In Plan Mode, Claude can only read files and use the AskUserQuestion tool — it can't edit or run anything. This forces deep analysis without the risk of premature implementation. Review the plan, refine it, then let Claude execute. 3. Implement — Execute with Verification After approving the plan, let Claude implement. Always tell it to write tests and verify its work. This is the single highest-leverage instruction you can give. implement the OAuth flow from your plan. write tests for the callback handler, run the test suite and fix any failures. 4. Commit — Ship with Context Let Claude create meaningful commits and PRs that include full context about what changed and why. commit with a descriptive message and open a PR Critical Principle Verification Is Everything ✅ The #1 Best Practice "The single highest-leverage thing you can do is give Claude a way to verify its own work." Include tests, expected outputs, or screenshot comparisons. When Claude can check itself, performance improves dramatically. If you can't verify it, don't ship it. — Anthropic Official Best Practices Verification Strategies Unit Tests "Write tests, run them, and fix any failures" — the most reliable verification loop. Type Checking Tell Claude to run npm run typecheck or mypy after changes. Add this to your CLAUDE.md. Linting Run npm run lint or equivalent. Claude will fix issues automatically if instructed. Screenshots For frontend work, use the Chrome extension or paste images to let Claude compare visual output against designs. Claude Code Mastery Guide · Source: Anthropic Best Practices CLAUDE.md — Your Project's AI Memory The most critical configuration file for Claude Code. It gives Claude persistent context about your project across every session. Why It Matters The Impact of CLAUDE.md ❌ Without CLAUDE.md Claude guesses your conventions. Uses wrong import styles. Doesn't know your test commands. Can't find your project structure. You repeat yourself every session. Wrong patterns. Wrong tools. ✅ With CLAUDE.md Claude follows your patterns from the first prompt. Uses correct styles, tools, and commands. Understands your architecture. Carries context across sessions. Consistent quality. Template What to Include # Code Style - Use ES modules (import/export), not CommonJS (require) - Destructure imports when possible - Use TypeScript strict mode - Prefer functional components over class components - Use kebab-case for file names # Workflow - Run `npm run typecheck` after making a series of code changes - Prefer running single tests, not the whole suite, for performance - Use `npm run lint:fix` before committing - Always run `npm test -- --related` for changed files # Architecture See @README.md for project overview and @package.json for available npm commands. # Key Patterns - API routes live in /src/api/routes/ - Database models use Prisma in /prisma/schema.prisma - Auth middleware is in /src/middleware/auth.ts - Error handling follows /src/utils/errors.ts patterns # Additional Instructions - Git workflow: @docs/git-instructions.md - API conventions: @docs/api-conventions.md - Personal overrides: @~/.claude/my-project-instructions.md # Compaction Rules When compacting, always preserve: - The full list of modified files - Any test commands used - Key architectural decisions made Configuration Hierarchical Locations Claude reads CLAUDE.md files from multiple locations, with more specific ones taking precedence. Location Scope Use Case ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md Global — all projects Personal preferences, universal conventions, preferred tools ./CLAUDE.md Project root Team conventions — check into git to share with team ./CLAUDE.local.md Project (personal) Your personal overrides — add to .gitignore ./src/CLAUDE.md Subdirectory Module-specific guidance — great for monorepos ../CLAUDE.md Parent directory Monorepo root conventions shared by sub-projects 💡 @ Imports Use @path/to/file syntax to import additional instruction files. This keeps your main CLAUDE.md lean while referencing detailed docs: See @README.md for project overview and @package.json for available npm commands. ⚠️ Common Mistake: Over-Specification If your CLAUDE.md is too long, Claude ignores important rules lost in the noise. Ruthlessly prune. If Claude already does something correctly without the instruction, delete it. Convert repetitive rules to hooks instead. Keep it focused on what Claude can't infer on its own. Advanced Dynamic CLAUDE.md with Hooks Use session hooks to inject dynamic context (recent commits, CI status, environment variables) into CLAUDE.md at session startup. # In a UserPromptSubmit hook, inject recent git context: echo "Recent commits: $(git log --oneline -5)" >> /tmp/claude-context.md # Claude reads this dynamically each session Claude Code Mastery Guide · Source: Anthropic Docs Prompting Like a Pro Specific, rich, contextual prompts are the difference between average and extraordinary results. Good vs Bad Specificity Changes Everything ❌ Vague Prompt "what would you improve in this file?" No file specified. No scope. No criteria. Claude has to guess everything. ✅ Specific Prompt "refactor the calculateTax function in @src/billing/tax.ts to handle EU VAT rules. Add unit tests covering zero-rate, standard-rate, and reverse-charge scenarios. Run the tests and fix failures." Exact file, clear task, specific test cases, verification built in. Techniques Context Injection Methods @ @ File References Reference files with @ instead of describing where code lives. Claude reads the file contents before responding. refactor @src/auth/oauth.ts following the patterns in @src/auth/saml.ts | Pipe In Data Send file contents, logs, error outputs, and diffs directly into Claude's input. # Pipe error logs cat error.log | claude "explain this error" # Pipe git diffs git diff main | claude -p "review this" # Pipe file lists find . -name "*.ts" | claude "which files handle auth?" 🖼️ Images Copy/paste or drag-and-drop images directly into the prompt. Perfect for UI bugs, design mockups, and error screenshots. [paste screenshot] Fix the layout to match this design. The button should be right-aligned. 🌐 URLs Give URLs for documentation and API references. Use /permissions to allowlist frequently-used domains for automatic access. 🔍 Let Claude Fetch Context Instead of providing everything upfront, tell Claude to pull context itself using Bash commands, MCP tools, or by reading files. Find all files that import from the billing module and understand how they use the calculateTax function. 🎯 Codebase Questions Ask Claude to understand code without changing it. Great for onboarding and knowledge transfer. How does logging work? What does async move { ... } do on line 134? Why does this code call foo() instead of bar()? Advanced Technique Let Claude Interview You For complex features where you haven't thought through all the details, let Claude ask the hard questions. I want to build [brief description]. Interview me in detail using the AskUserQuestion tool. Ask about technical implementation, UI/UX, edge cases, concerns, and tradeoffs. Don't ask obvious questions — dig into the hard parts I might not have considered. Keep interviewing until we've covered everything, then write a complete spec to SPEC.md. 🧠 Why This Works Developers often start coding before thinking through edge cases. The interview technique forces you to consider authentication flows, error handling, race conditions, and UX decisions before any code is written. The resulting spec becomes a better prompt for implementation. Claude Code Mastery Guide · Source: Anthropic Docs Context Management The hidden superpower that separates power users from beginners. Claude's performance degrades when its context fills with irrelevant information. Core Strategies Keep Context Clean & Focused 🧹 /clear — Reset Between Tasks Use /clear between unrelated tasks. This fully resets the context window. Long sessions with mixed context significantly reduce Claude's performance. # After finishing one task: /clear # Now start a completely new task 📦 /compact — Compress Context When auto-compaction triggers, Claude summarizes what matters most. For more control, run it manually with focus instructions: /compact Focus on the API changes /compact Keep the migration plan and all file paths /compact Preserve test commands and architectural decisions ⏪ Rewind — Checkpoint Restore Press Esc + Esc or run /rewind to open the rewind menu: Restore previous conversation and code state Summarize from a selected message forward Keep earlier context intact while compressing recent messages 🔍 Subagents for Investigation Heavy research tasks can fill your main context. Offload them to subagents that search, explore, and report back without polluting your primary window. use subagents to investigate how our auth system handles token refresh, and whether we have any existing OAuth utilities I should reuse ✋ Esc — Course-Correct Early Press Esc to stop Claude mid-action. Context is preserved, so you can redirect immediately. Don't let Claude go far down the wrong path. ↩️ Resume Sessions Resume previous work without losing context. Name sessions with /rename for easy retrieval. claude --continue # Most recent claude --resume # Pick from list Reference Context Actions Quick Reference Action How When to Use Esc Stop mid-action, preserve context Claude is heading the wrong direction Esc + Esc Open rewind/checkpoint menu Restore previous state or selective summarize /clear Full context reset Between completely unrelated tasks /compact [focus] Compress with instructions Context getting large, auto-compaction not enough /rewind Menu to restore checkpoints Undo failed approaches or bad paths "Undo that" Tell Claude to revert Quick rollback of recent code changes --continue Resume latest session Continue where you left off --resume Pick from sessions list Resume a specific named conversation /rename [name] Name current session Create bookmarks for long-running work 🧠 Pro Tip: Compaction Rules in CLAUDE.md Add instructions to your CLAUDE.md like: "When compacting, always preserve the full list of modified files and any test commands." This ensures critical context survives auto-summarization, so you never lose track of what's been changed. 📝 Handoff Documents For long-running projects, before /clear , ask Claude: "Write a handoff document summarizing all work, decisions, remaining tasks, and files changed." Start the new session with that summary as input. Community-proven technique for preserving context across fresh sessions. Claude Code Mastery Guide · Source: Anthropic Docs Extending Claude Code Skills, Hooks, MCP Servers, Custom Subagents, and Plugins — unlock Claude's full potential with the extensibility system. Extension System Five Ways to Extend 🎯 Skills — Reusable Slash Commands Skills are SKILL.md files in .claude/skills/ that define reusable workflows invoked via /slash-commands . They're the most accessible way to extend Claude Code. Example: Fix GitHub Issues --- name: fix-issue description: Fix a GitHub issue disable-model-invocation: true --- Analyze and fix the GitHub issue: $ARGUMENTS. 1. Use `gh issue view` to get the issue details 2. Understand the problem described in the issue 3. Search the codebase for relevant files 4. Implement the necessary changes to fix the issue 5. Write and run tests to verify the fix 6. Ensure code passes linting and type checking 7. Create a descriptive commit message 8. Push and create a PR Usage: /fix-issue 1234 Example: API Conventions --- name: api-conventions description: REST API design conventions for our services --- # API Conventions - Use kebab-case for URL paths - Use camelCase for JSON properties - Always include pagination for list endpoints - Version APIs in the URL path (/v1/, /v2/) Key Concepts • Skills are loaded on-demand to minimize token usage • Use $ARGUMENTS to accept arguments from the slash command • Set disable-model-invocation: true for deterministic scripts that don't need AI reasoning • Can include scripts/, examples/, and resources/ subdirectories ⚡ Hooks — Automated Event Triggers Shell scripts that run automatically when specific events occur during a session. Configure via /hooks command or directly in .claude/settings.json . Hook Events Event When It Fires Use Case PreToolUse Before Claude executes a tool Validation, security blocks PostToolUse After tool execution completes Auto-formatting, logging UserPromptSubmit Before Claude processes your prompt Inject dynamic context Notification When Claude needs your input Desktop alerts, sounds Desktop Notification Hook (macOS) osascript -e 'display notification "Claude Code needs your attention" with title "Claude Code"' Security: Hooks can block dangerous commands or modifications to sensitive files. They provide a deterministic control layer over Claude's behavior. 🔌 MCP Servers — External System Connections The Model Context Protocol connects Claude to external systems — databases, APIs, monitoring tools, issue trackers, documentation sites. claude mcp add What MCP Enables Query your production database directly Fetch Sentry error details and stack traces Read and search Notion/Confluence documentation Interact with Jira/Linear issues Browse documentation sites Access any API through custom MCP servers MCP is an open-source standard — any tool can expose an MCP interface for Claude to use. 🤖 Custom Subagents — Specialized AI Workers Create purpose-specific agents in .claude/agents/ . Each subagent has its own system prompt, tool access, and can even use different models (e.g., Opus for deep review). --- name: security-reviewer description: Reviews code for security vulnerabilities tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash model: opus --- You are a senior security engineer. Review code for: - Injection vulnerabilities (SQL, XSS, command injection) - Authentication and authorization flaws - Secrets or credentials in code - Insecure data handling Provide specific line references and suggested fixes. Key Benefits Isolated context: Subagent work doesn't pollute your main conversation Specialized prompts: Each agent focuses on one expertise area Tool restriction: Limit what each agent can access for safety Model selection: Use Opus for deep analysis, Sonnet for speed 🧩 Plugins — Community Extensions Install community-built plugins with /plugin . Plugins bundle skills, subagents, hooks, and resources into shareable packages. Code Intelligence Plugin: Adds precise "go to definition" and "find references" navigation for your programming language Frontend Design Plugin: Enhances UI/UX code generation with design system knowledge Browse and discover plugins from the community marketplace Decision Guide Which Extension to Use? Need Use Why Reusable workflow Skill Slash command invocation, filesystem-based Auto-run on events Hook Deterministic, no AI reasoning needed External data access MCP Server Standard protocol for tool connection Specialized AI task Subagent Isolated context, custom system prompt Shareable package Plugin Bundles multiple extensions together Claude Code Mastery Guide · Source: Anthropic Docs Automation & CI/CD Run Claude headlessly in scripts, CI/CD pipelines, and batch operations at scale. Headless Mode claude -p — Non-Interactive Execution Process prompts without an interactive session. Perfect for scripting and automation. # One-off queries claude -p "Explain what this project does" # Structured JSON output for scripts claude -p "List all API endpoints" --output-format json # Streaming for real-time processing claude -p "Analyze this log file" --output-format stream-json # Plain text output (default) claude -p "Summarize recent changes" --output-format text Batch Operations Fan Out Across Files Generate a Task List list all 2,000 Python files that need migrating Write a Script to Loop for file in $(cat files.txt); do claude -p "Migrate $file from React to Vue. Return OK or FAIL." \ --allowedTools "Edit,Bash(git commit *)" done Test on a Few, Then Scale Use --allowedTools to scope permissions. Use --verbose for debugging during testing phase. CI/CD Integration GitHub Actions & GitLab 🐙 GitHub Actions An official Claude Code GitHub Action brings AI automation to your workflows: Auto-review PRs for bugs, style, and security Generate test scaffolds for changed files Implement features from issue descriptions Respond to @claude mentions in PRs and issues Create detailed changelogs from commits Store your Anthropic API key as a repository secret. Trigger workflows on pull_request events or @claude mentions. 🦊 GitLab CI/CD Integrate Claude Code into GitLab pipelines for AI-powered merge request assistance: Auto-propose merge requests from issue descriptions Respond to @claude in MR comments Run automated code review on diffs Generate documentation for changed code Store the Anthropic API key as a masked, protected CI/CD variable. Use event-driven triggers for MR and issue comments. Unix Utility Pipe, Chain & Integrate Use Claude as a standard Unix utility in your existing command-line workflows. # Monitor logs for anomalies tail -f app.log | claude -p "Slack me if you see any anomalies" # Automate translations in CI claude -p "translate new strings into French and raise a PR for review" # Security review changed files git diff main --name-only | claude -p "review these changed files for security issues" # Chain with other commands claude -p "your prompt" --output-format json | jq '.result' | your_command # Code review as verification step claude -p "Review @src/auth.ts for injection vulnerabilities. Output 'PASS' or 'FAIL: reason'" 🔒 Safe Autonomous Mode For fully autonomous operation, --dangerously-skip-permissions bypasses all prompts. Only use inside sandboxed environments (Docker containers, CI runners). Parallel Sessions Git Worktrees — Isolated Parallel Work Each Claude session gets its own isolated git worktree — no merge conflicts between parallel agents working on the same project. # Start Claude in a named worktree # Creates .claude/worktrees/feature-auth/ with a new branch claude --worktree feature-auth # Start another session in a separate worktree claude --worktree bugfix-123 # Auto-generate a worktree name claude --worktree # Creates something like "bright-running-fox" How It Works Each worktree lives in <repo>/.claude/worktrees/<name> A new branch worktree-<name> is created automatically Full filesystem isolation — no conflicts between sessions Cleanup available for completed worktrees Use Cases Work on a feature while a bug fix runs in parallel Test Opus vs Sonnet on the same problem simultaneously Run code review in one session while implementing in another Explore alternative implementation strategies concurrently Experimental Agent Teams Coordinate multiple Claude instances with shared tasks, messaging, and a team lead. Look for edge cases, race conditions, and consistency with our existing middleware patterns." Session A: "Here's the review feedback: [Session B output]. Address these issues." 🖥️ Desktop App Sessions Manage multiple local sessions visually. Each session gets its own isolated worktree. See diffs and changes in a graphical interface. 🌐 Claude Code on the Web Run on Anthropic's secure cloud infrastructure in isolated VMs. No local resources consumed. Restrict tools Claude can use (e.g., "Edit,Bash(git commit *)") --dangerously-skip-permissions Skip all permission prompts (sandbox only!) --verbose Show detailed output for debugging claude mcp add Add an MCP server connection Quick Prompts Common One-Liners # Explore a codebase claude "give me an overview of this codebase" claude "trace the login process from front-end to database" # Bug fixing claude "I'm seeing an error when I run npm test" claude "suggest a few ways to fix the @ts-ignore in user.ts" # Tests claude "find functions in NotificationsService.swift not covered by tests" claude "write tests for the auth module, run them, fix failures" # Refactoring claude "refactor utils.js to use ES2024 features, maintain same behavior" claude "find deprecated API usage in our codebase" # Documentation claude "add JSDoc comments to undocumented functions in auth.js" # Git claude "commit with a descriptive message and open a PR" claude "summarize the changes I've made to the authentication module" Claude Code Mastery Guide · Source: Anthropic Docs Anti-Patterns & Pitfalls Five common failure patterns that derail productivity — and how to fix them. Directly from Anthropic's official best practices. Failure Patterns Avoid These Traps 🍳 The Kitchen Sink Session What happens: You start with one task, ask Claude something unrelated, then go back to the first task. The context fills with irrelevant information, and Claude's performance degrades. ✅ Fix Use /clear between unrelated tasks. Every single time. If you need to context-switch, clear first. 🔄 Correcting Over and Over What happens: Claude does something wrong, you correct it, it's still wrong, you correct again. The context becomes polluted with failed approaches, making each attempt worse. ✅ Fix After two failed corrections , stop. Run /clear and write a better initial prompt that incorporates what you learned from the failures. A fresh start with a better prompt beats repeated corrections. 📜 The Over-Specified CLAUDE.md What happens: Your CLAUDE.md grows to hundreds of lines. Important rules get buried in noise. Claude ignores critical instructions because they're lost in the volume. ✅ Fix Ruthlessly prune. If Claude already does something correctly without the instruction, delete it. Convert repetitive patterns to hooks. Keep CLAUDE.md focused on what Claude can't infer on its own. 👁️ The Trust-Then-Verify Gap What happens: Claude produces a plausible-looking implementation that doesn't handle edge cases. You trust it because it looks right, but it breaks in production. ✅ Fix Always provide verification. Tell Claude to write tests, run them, and fix failures. If you can't verify the output (no tests, no type checking, no screenshots), don't ship it . 🌊 The Infinite Exploration What happens: You ask Claude to "investigate" or "look into" something without scoping it. Claude reads hundreds of files, filling the context window with exploration data. ✅ Fix Scope investigations narrowly: "Look at /src/auth to understand token refresh" (not "investigate our auth system"). For broad research, use subagents so exploration doesn't consume your main context. Develop Your Intuition When to Intervene Experience is learning when to let Claude run versus when to course-correct. Here are signals to watch for. 🟢 Let Claude Continue When... It's following your plan methodically It's running tests and fixing failures iteratively The file changes align with your expectations It's asking clarifying questions instead of guessing 🔴 Intervene When... It's reading dozens of unrelated files It's rewriting something that already works It's ignoring your architectural constraints The same error has been corrected twice It's generating boilerplate you didn't ask for Claude Code Mastery Guide · Source: Anthropic Best Practices Community Wisdom Battle-tested patterns from developers, Anthropic engineers, and the broader community. (2) Run two sessions — one writes tests, another writes code.
